findings.issue: Brooke's pitch names "sandwiches", which reads as a want, but no review confirms or rules out sandwiches. The only sandwich in any review is Griddle House's grilled cheese, so the line nudges a careful player toward the healthy-vibe decoy. Not a rule for level_04 (the no-unconfirmable-asks rule starts at level_06), so this is noted for consistency only.
findings.suggested_fix: "love that. ok, my pitch: cafe lunch. coffee and good chats"

findings.issue: The single vibe:healthy need is split into two asks ("nothing greasy or oily" and "something fresh! salads, grain bowls"), which can read as two separate requirements. The one-wish-per-soft-need rule starts at level_06, so this is only a note here.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge into one line: "one thing for me: nothing greasy or oily. something fresh and light!" and drop or untag script[6].

findings.issue: "The Nutty Mug" announces its peanut trap from the card alone, before any review is read (the review even says "Lives up to the name"). The neutral-decoy-name rule only applies from level_06, and the name is a fixed registry field, so no change is required; just avoid reusing this pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: If the venue is ever replaced, use a neutral name such as "The Corner Mug", and drop "Lives up to the name" from the review.

findings.issue: "Griddle House" hints at greasy food, so the healthy decoy is partly readable from its name. Allowed for level_04 (rule starts at level_06); noted only.
findings.suggested_fix: No change for level_04; in later levels give vibe decoys neutral names.

findings.issue: The perfect reaction almost copies level_02's: Maya's "and it's CHEAP?? the trip fund..." and Cyrus's "No peanuts ... on the menu. Well chosen." The puzzle shape (peanut trap, $$ twin, Maya's "one dollar sign" line) also echoes level_02, so the repeated wording makes it feel recycled.
findings.suggested_fix: Maya: "under ten bucks for coffee AND lunch?? the coast is getting closer". Cyrus: "Peanut-free kitchen, confirmed with the barista. Excellent work."

findings.issue: Maya's line on a partial result uses HAPPY; the bible's Scoring table gives ANNOYED or SURPRISED portraits for a partial. Her upbeat line works in character, but the emotion clashes with the result screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the text, set emotion to SURPRISED, or rephrase: "cheap, sure. but brooke is sipping coffee while i eat hash browns. awkward" with ANNOYED.

findings.issue: Cyrus lists "even the granola", which no review mentions (reviews cite smoothies, bowls and bakes). It doesn't contradict anything but could match the reviews more closely.
findings.suggested_fix: "There are peanuts in nearly everything here. The smoothies, the bowls, even the baked goods."

summary: A clean, warm introduction for Brooke: every scored constraint (cafe craving, healthy, $ budget, peanut allergy) is stated plainly, there is no recap list, voices match the Cast, and the reviews evidence each deciding attribute without contradicting the chat. Continuity with level_02 and level_05 holds (Cyrus's lab section, Maya's coast trip). The suggestions are mostly level_06-era rules this level predates (the sandwiches ask, the split healthy wish, telling decoy names) plus perfect-outcome wording that repeats level_02.
